### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f7fdd002130a34ce24f735733c2642538914af9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2496f6b3a24f91da5083d6381c0fe365ad30173b` — the merge of head `f278fece6f2227841ace298611c7444c63319422` into base `3f7fdd002130a34ce24f735733c2642538914af9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2496f6b3a24f91da5083d6381c0fe365ad30173b && git checkout 2496f6b3a24f91da5083d6381c0fe365ad30173b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3f7fdd002130a34ce24f735733c2642538914af9 f278fece6f2227841ace298611c7444c63319422 && git checkout -B drift-repro 3f7fdd002130a34ce24f735733c2642538914af9 && git merge --no-ff f278fece6f2227841ace298611c7444c63319422

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3f7fdd002130a34ce24f735733c2642538914af9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f278fece6f2227841ace298611c7444c63319422`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/formula/src/cel-engine.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/meta-flow-condition-record-date-text.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-registration-schema-e2e.test.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.flow-condition-record-date-arithmetic-refused.ts + skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md, content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx (both read on `main`, not in the diff). The changeset is read for ② only.

Inputs: card #34946 with its 9 comments, PR #36333 body and 7 comments (no review, no inline comment), the net diff `origin/main...f278fece6f` (8 files, +386/-9, merge-base `28ba01fe69`), and the check-runs on the head: 60 success, 13 skipped, 0 failed, 0 pending. `main` has not touched `cel-engine.ts` or `validate.ts` since the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept-set, flow conditions (`scope: 'flattened'`: start, edge and `decision` conditions at `os validate` / `os build`, the runtime publish door, and the `validate_expression` flow-condition site): `record.FIELD` / `previous.FIELD` of a `date` or `datetime` field in `+ - * / %` against a number goes from no finding to an `error` under `date-arithmetic-run-fails` / `date-arithmetic-run-may-fail`. Right, and a narrowing: `firstTypeMismatch`'s record-root pass (`cel-engine.ts` :1432-1442) answers `date-arith` when the root typing's first operator fault is `isDateArith`.
- Outcome arm: a root read takes `dateArm(scope, faultOutcome, false)` (`validate.ts` :603), so it keeps `run-fails` where bare names are unproven or shadowed, and `run-may-fail` where no outcome is declared. Right: the same rule the root read's type mismatch (#30025) and date-text verdicts already follow.
- No new refusal code, no new params key, no new export: `firstTypeMismatch`'s return type is unchanged (`root` was already optional on it, now also set on `date-arith`). Its three callers are all in `validate.ts`; none keyed on `root` being absent for `date-arith`. Right.
- Record-scoped sites (formula fields, validation rules, the flow value envelope) are untouched: the new branch sits behind `scope !== 'flattened'`. Right.
- One side effect the PR does not name, judged right: the #30025 swap in `typeSoundnessIssue` (:570-577) re-asks with every bare name shadowed, and that second ask can now return a root `date-arith`. Under unproven bare names, a source holding a bare text mismatch and a root date arithmetic moves from the bare warning with no outcome to the root's `date-arithmetic-run-fails` error. It is inside the declared narrowing (the root read is proven to fault) but no pin names it (see N3).
- `registerFlow` stays advisory, the evaluator is unchanged, a stored flow still registers. Right, and pinned by the service-automation test.
- No double report: `recordRootDateTextIssue` stands down on the shape through `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith`, and is only reached when `firstTypeMismatch` answered null. Right for the single-fault shapes; S1 below is where the two typings disagree.

### ② Semver level

`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and in the changeset; `!` title; `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`; BREAKING banner with a FROM → TO table; marker `adr-0087: registered flow-condition-record-date-arithmetic-refused`, and the entry of that id is in the diff. `@objectstack/formula` minor matches what the diff publishes: a behavioural narrowing of `validateExpression` with no API change, at the level the #34935 and #36207 precedents took. `@objectstack/spec` minor covers the new migration entry. `lint`, `runtime` and `service-automation` change in test files only and owe no entry. `Check Changeset` is success at the head. The level holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- open_questions 1 (Metadata-protocol `none` or `narrowed`): answered B at this head, `narrowed` with minor; claim revision 7075338493 records it. Agreed: a previously publishable condition is refused.
- open_questions 2 (a permanent publish-door pin): answered B at this head; the runtime describe asserts `INVALID_METADATA` / 422 with the draft left, and the control publishes. The file-surface extension is recorded in 7075338493.
- Dev flag, bare and root date arithmetic in one source under unproven names reports the bare one at `run-may-fail`: answered, accepted deviation (N2). Still an error.
- Dev flag, the refusing door is `publishMetaItem` and not `registerFlow`: answered, a correction of the dispatch's wording and pinned on both sides.
- L1-a R1 (battery pinned to the head): closed by 7076550688, ACCEPT 7076562103.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff is an authoring-time type check; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.
- Nothing escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. On `main`, `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` :167 says "No date arithmetic. The build refuses `date + n` and `end - start`" with no site excepted, and `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` :253 lists date arithmetic against a number as refused because the value is text at run time. No doc, skill or example on `main` writes a date field plus a number through `record.` or `previous.` as a working shape. The bare name was already refused in the same condition, and the root read reaches the evaluator as the same text: the formula test evaluates all three spellings over a row and each answers `ok: false`. So the accepted-before shape was never a capability, it was a condition that failed every run.

Tried to break it:
- A false refusal of something the runtime answers. The branch fires only when the bare typing found no fault to report and the root typing's first fault is date or duration arithmetic against a number. Ordering against `today()`, equality, concatenation with text, and arithmetic against a number field (typed `dyn`) do not reach it; the controls pin the first, and the rest follow from `isDateArith` and `UNSOUND_OVERLOAD_RE`. None found.
- A wrong arm. For the root branch to fire, the bare typing either had no fault or its first fault was one the date-text re-check stood down; in both cases the date-arithmetic fault involves a root read, so giving it the row's arm is sound. A shadowing flow variable changes only the bare typing. None found.
- A second finding. Single-fault shapes yield exactly one; pinned at formula, lint and the door.
- Datetime control: `datetime` is typed Timestamp exactly as `date`, the bare name was refused already, and the root verdict equals the bare one with the reference swapped. Holds.
- ADR-0087 entry: a structured TODO is the right kind, since span or shift is the author's intent and is not recorded. Surface, replacement and acceptance criteria agree with the code and the changeset.

S1 (should-fix) — non-blocking, carry on a follow-up card; it does not block this landing. A residual acceptance of the narrowed shape, by code read (not run; the follow-up measures it first). Source: a bare date field ordered against a text literal, AND-ed before a root read's arithmetic, i.e. `due_date` compared with `"2026-01-01"` and then `record.due_date + 1` compared with a number. The bare pass's first fault is the Timestamp-against-string ordering, which `confirmAgainstDateText` stands down, so it answers null. The root pass types bare names and roots together (`buildTypedEnv(bareTypes, 'flattened', 'timestamp', fieldCelTypes)`), meets that same ordering first, finds it is not `isDateArith`, and answers null. `recordRootDateTextIssue` then asks `recordRootReadsFaultDateArith`, which types the roots alone (bare names `{}`), meets `record.due_date + 1` first, and stands down because the shape "is answered" by `firstTypeMismatch`. Neither reports, and the flow still faults on every run. The two functions disagree on what the first fault is because one types the bare names and the other does not. The all-root spelling of the same compound is caught (as `date-text-arithmetic`), and so is the all-bare one; only the mixed one falls through. It is not a regression, since `main` passes it too, and the card's Done-when shapes are all met; it is the narrowing left incomplete at one seam. Fix direction: when the root pass's first fault is not date arithmetic, ask the roots-only typing as well, or have the stand-down ask `firstTypeMismatch`'s actual answer.

Nits (no effect on correctness or the contract; accepted deviations or the same follow-up card):
- N1: `offendingRecordRead` names the first Timestamp field read through a root in field-map order, which can be a read other than the one in the arithmetic (an ordering of `record.created_at` before `previous.due_date + 1` can name `record.created_at`). The PR states it as best effort, as for the bare name.
- N2: the bare-and-root pair under unproven names reports the bare verdict at `run-may-fail` (the dev's own note).
- N3: the #30025 swap now reaching a root `date-arith` (① above) has no pin.

No must-fix. One should-fix, S1, non-blocking and carried to a follow-up card by the landing seat.
